items.title: Nested Link Display and Reference Issues in Logseq (Current Version and DB Test) - Hoping for a "For good" Fix
items.body:
> ---
> ### **Description**
> Nested page links and references in Logseq exhibit several display and structural issues, particularly when using complex nested brackets. These problems persist across both the current version (Logseq 0.9.x) and the DB test version (January 2025). The issues affect link rendering, reference creation, and graph consistency.
> 
> 
> ---
> ### **Current Behavior**
> #### **Display Issues**
> - Nested links such as `[[[[Mon]] [[nom]] de [[nœud]] dans [[mon]] [[graphe]] dans [[Logseq]]]]` fail to render correctly in the journal view.
>   - Links like `[[Mon]] [[]]` are not displayed at all, as shown in the screenshots.
> 
> 
> ---
> ### **Steps to Reproduce**
> 1. Create a block with a nested link, such as `[[[[Mon]] [[nom]] de [[nœud]] dans [[mon]] [[graphe]] dans [[Logseq]]]]`.
> 2. Exit edit mode.
> 3. Observe:
>    - Incorrect rendering of the link in the journal view.
>    - Missing or malformed references in linked pages.
>    - Inconsistent behavior when navigating via graph view versus text links.
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f699268f-9c67-4b4a-bb8b-d7be39760c80)
> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9fc3a0a-d530-4e04-a1b5-d14fe7b0e527)

> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c455de0-c657-42b4-b8a6-21368589ffd2)
> 
> 
> ---
> ### **Expected Behavior**
> 1. Nested page links should render accurately in all views (journal, page, graph).
> 2. References should resolve correctly and consistently across all navigation methods.
> 3. Graph view should properly represent nested structures without losing hierarchy or alias relationships.
> 
> 
> ---
> ### **Technical Details**
> - **Current Version:** Logseq 0.10.10. **Web DB Test Version:** Latest build as of 19 January 2025
> - **Platforms:** Issue observed in web-based version
> - **Related Issues:** #10254, #506, #9541, #7085, #7951, #2954, #3245, #3234, #1489, #1376, #1351, #975, #188, https://github.com/logseq/logseq/discussions/7974, #101, https://github.com/logseq/db-test/issues/111, https://github.com/logseq/logseq/issues?q=+nested+in%3Atitle+is%3Aopen+ .............................................
> 
> 
> ---
> ### **Impact**
> These issues significantly disrupt workflows involving:
> - Complex knowledge graphs
> - Hierarchical data organization
> - Academic research and project management
> - Cross-referenced documentation systems
> - Me crying for the last two years ^^
> ---

items.title: Show warning or support multiple logseq tabs in the same browser profile

labels.name: :type/enhancement
labels.description: Enhancement to product. Does not affect the overall basic use.

items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently logseq does not handle having multiple tabs (in the same browser profile) open to the same repository. It easily gets into an inconsistent state where changes in one of the tabs can be lost.

This does make sense given logseq's architecture, but we should make sure that it does not lead to data loss.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Some kind of lock in local storage that warns a user if he opens two tabs to the same repo. Either refusing to open a new instance to the same repo, or opening a read-only version.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Ideally, the different instances should be able to stay in sync because they both have access to the same indexeddb serialized version of the datascript database (or something like that, I'm not 100% clear on the architecture). If that can be achieved, it would of course be much better than just refusing to open the same repo in a different tab.

Another possible option could be to find a way to sandbox the local storage/indexeddb data to each tab, so that two tabs work independently, and both sync independently to github.

(PS: Let me know if you would like a reproducible way to get logseq into an inconsistent state with two tabs open, but in general it seems to be enough to just write something in both tabs, and only one of them will be correctly synced to github)

items.title: Intermittent Data Loss

labels.name: need-to-reproduce
labels.description: More clues are required to reproduce the issue.

items.body:
### What happened?

I (as a Windows user) and others using a MAC device (per Discord comments) have been experiencing unexplained data loss in Logseq.  This has been happening since at least version 0.6.2 and still occurs in 0.7.0. Some "details" that might be helpful can be viewed in the Discord #bugs channel inside a thread "Lost info".  Essentially Logseq is running, working fine, and then data in the app suddenly "disappears". It is never ALL of the data, just perhaps 30-40% of it, so the occurrence isn't obvious to the user. We started noticing it because queries inside our Logseq data began to fail - i.e. produce obviously false results.  In a couple of cases, actual MD files were lost.  But 98% of the time, you could "force stop" Logseq, restart it, then do a re-index and get most / all of your data back.  This occurred on a "network isolated" Windows PC with Logseq data being stored on a local hard disk. The problem, of course, was that until you "noticed" the issue - any data you provided to someone from Logseq was quite likely faulty.

First, I must say, I'm not an IT person. So I cannot provide much technical feedback.  However, I do have a large IT team that works for me and they have solved the issue for our specific case - which I will try to describe below.  However, my developers said I should pass the info along because others using commercial "sync" products might likely face similar issues.

In our cases, data is stored locally via something called a "User Mode File System".  This allows the IT guys to do backups and create the necessary audit trails, etc.  When out "backup process" ran, it generates a "dokan release event" and then a "dokan start event".  This supposedly happens within about 10 seconds.  I have no idea what those are - but if those occur while Logseq is running, Logseq seems to "notice it" and starts deleting things.  The "fix" for us was to kill the Logseq task before running backup.  Doing so has fixed the issue for us - and no data has randomly disappeared since we started force closing the app before running backup.

So things are fine here, and no action is necessary.  I was just passing along the info as requested in case it helps solve a similar "mystery" for some other user.

### Reproduce the Bug

Have Logseq up and running.  It doesn't matter what screen you are on.
Generate a user mode file system "dokan release event".
Generate a user mode file system "dokan start event".
Check Logseq "Developer Mode" and you will see LOTS of "Deleted Pages" and other technical messages.

### Expected Behavior

I would expect the application not to perform "random delete actions" when backup was run.

### Screenshots

See Discord info referenced above...

### Desktop Platform Information

Windows 10 Logseq 0.6.2 - 0.7.0

### Mobile Platform Information

N/A

### Additional Context

_No response_

items.title: Mobile logseq is having a hard time tracking files synced with icloud.

labels.description: More clues are required to reproduce the issue.

items.body:
### Search first

- [X] I searched and no similar issues were found

### What Happened?

I use logseq across mobile, desktop, and ipad, syncing with icloud. icloud syncing works fine, but logseq can't regularly track changes to pages or even the pages at all. 

This manifests in two specific ways:

Pretty much daily, I populate my daily journal page on desktop. Later in the day, I will go to the same page on mobile and it will be empty, until I start typing and I get a screen that shows me two conflicting versions of the page to choose from, one from logseq (which is empty) and one from disk (which is populated with what I put there on desktop that morning). I choose the version on disk, expecting this to resolve confusion for logseq. But pretty regularly, this will confuse logseq and lead to some loading screen, after which the page is blank again and I have to go through the same process. 

Relatedly, several pages that I know exist (because I've used them for a long time and they exist on both desktop and ipad) don't exist in logseq on mobile. I know this because the references to blocks in those pages appear broken only on mobile. Sure enough, when I go to the page with the missing blocks, it's empty. As mentioned above, my mobile logseq has a really hard time keeping up with the syncs, so I will start typing on the empty page and suddenly this conflicting versions page will pop up where I'm supposed to choose between the version of the page on disk (which is nonempty) and the version in logseq (which has whatever random stuff I just typed), and I will choose the populated version. At this point, the references are no longer broken. 

The reason I'm even going to the lengths of reporting this is that it's a regular, recurrent problem. The same pages keep disappearing from logseq even though they're there on disk, and it's a hassle to force a version control conflict between disk and logseq every time I have broken references.

### Reproduce the Bug

I think if this were a bug that happened broadly, I would have been able to find another issue/it would have been resolved in 0.8.18, so I don't know how to instruct you to recreate it, except by doing the following:

1. Find a page in logseq that is empty/doesn't exist, but that you are sure exists on disk
2. Start typing until you get a conflict resolution screen.

### Expected Behavior

I expect logseq to track pages that are on disk, but it doesn't seem to.

### Screenshots


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13025465/228018511-0a3d883e-bdb7-4492-987e-71254434fe59.MP4



### Desktop or Mobile Platform Information

_No response_

### Additional Context

macOS 13.2.1, Desktop App v0.8.18
iPhone 13 Pro Max, iOS 16.3.1, v0.8.18

### Are you willing to submit a PR? If you know how to fix the bug.

- [ ] I'm willing to submit a PR (Thank you!)

items.title: Wrong configuration caused multiple notes in LogSeq not written to disk

labels.name: :type/question
labels.description: Not bug, closed at will. Frequently asked ones would be collected in Logseq Forum's FAQ section.

items.body:
### What happened?

Hi, first of all, I love LogSeq very much and appreciate greatly the work being done on it!!

**This issue is highly important to me as it might cause me (or others) to lose note content.**

I have noticed that with multiple notes (stored locally) their contents have not always been written to disk. They persist when LogSeq is closed and re-opened but **only a few lines of the note (the first few lines I would have written) appear on disk** when I open it in VSCode (or inspect the files uploaded via git to GitHub - which is how I noticed this - when I was trying to look at a notes' contents on github.com on my phone). I do have git auto commit enabled and push regularly and I had thought it was working fine, giving me a good backup of my notes but this is not working as planned.

I am not sure how to reproduce the main bug, but one other thing I have noticed that may be related is this warning message that pops up when I make a new page (within LogSeq):

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5212453/152521065-19c62e61-f0e7-4957-a5cc-9a689d8ff880.png)

To reproduce the above, possibly related issue:
1. Go to LogSeq
2. Create a new page and type a few lines
3. Wait a moment
4. The error should pop up

I have wondered whether this occurs due to the notes being stored in a DropBox folder, but I am not sure. I thought it was relatively harmless as once dismissed LogSeq stops complaining. But now I wonder if it's related to the main issue of the notes not being written to disk as what is written to disk successfully seems like it could be the same as what was already written at the time of the error message popping up.


I am now concerned that I am going to lose a range of content I have written as I don't know all the files which are affected by the main issue. I am also wary of taking certain actions to debug things in case I lose my notes that are not saved to the filesystem in the process, as I'm sure you can understand.

Please help! :slightly_smiling_face: Please let me know you have any insights into how to best fix this for my situation. Thanks very much.

I am running LogSeq 0.5.1 on NixOS (a Linux distro).

### Reproduce the Bug

I have included how to reproduce (as best as I can) in context in the previous answer.

### Expected Behavior

When the LogSeq editor shows that content is there, it should immediately (or very soon) be written to disk, or at the very least on the close of LogSeq it should be written to disk.

The git auto-commit should be committing content that I write in notes at the specified interval and not missing large portions of content.

When I write a new note, I should not get the error pop-up that I mentioned.

### Screenshots

The one relevant screenshot is 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5212453/152523249-8541f975-b8cf-4efc-a1c3-9f072c521beb.png)


### Desktop Platform Information

- OS: NixOS
- Browser: (I am using the LogSeq Desktop App)
- Version: 0.5.1

_No response_

### Additional Context

I use LogSeq to take notes related to my PhD study (and for aspects of my personal life), I really would not like to lose content...

items.title: pages-metadata.edn data structure does not scale with distributed workflow

labels.name: :type/enhancement
labels.description: Enhancement to product. Does not affect the overall basic use.

items.body:
**Describe the bug**
After a few months of using git to sync Logseq on two computers, resolving merge conflicts in `pages-metadata.edn` without data loss is proving to be a challenge. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Use Logseq daily on two or more computers with the same git repository as a database until `pages-metadata.edn` is ~= 3k lines. Do not put `pages-metadata.edn` in `.gitignore`.
2. Skip merging for a few days while continuing to use Logseq on both computers, making new block refs and embeds, expanding and contracting existing nodes, adding new pages, and renaming some existing pages
3. Attempt a merge
4. See hundreds of merge conflicts
6. Try accepting just one side of the merge conflicts
7. Open logseq, and see a bunch of broken references
8. Undo the merge
9. Move `pages-metadata.edn` to `pages-metadata.edn.bak` and open up logseq; observe that the file is recreated, but the created and updated dates are not accurate.

**Expected behavior**
1. If `pages-metadata.edn` is deleted and recreated, the created and updated dates should be taken from the page files metadata.
2. So far, `pages-metadata.edn` only contains name, modification date, and creation date. I would actually expect this information to be taken from and persisted in the page files themselves. If there is a performance or other reason why this should be persisted outside of the files, then the data structure that stores this information should scale to a large size and continue to function in a distributed workflow without the need for an unmanageable number of manual merge conflict resolutions, each of which could lead to data loss or corruption. 

See [`davclark`'s suggestion](https://discuss.logseq.com/t/format-pages-metadata-edn-before-saving/2506/8?u=codekiln) in logseq discuss. I'll resist the urge to research algorithmic precedent or improvise one here, but Like `davclark` I'd be happy to help in designing a data structure and algorithm. 

**Screenshots**
![image of 100s of merge conflicts](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/140930/149599099-a92c6447-3817-4a4a-a8a3-9198d7a43f0c.png)

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Mac
 - Version 0.5.8

**Additional context**
This has been discussed a bit at discuss.logseq.com: 

1. https://discuss.logseq.com/t/format-pages-metadata-edn-before-saving/2506/8?u=codekiln
2. [How important is pages-metadata.edn? - Questions & Help - Logseq](https://discuss.logseq.com/t/how-important-is-pages-metadata-edn/2896/2)
